name: Amanta Healthcare Ltd
title: Amanta Healthcare Ltd - 544502 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: SteriPort Line 3 commissioning slipped one quarter to late August on civil delays, pushing ~INR70 crores of contribution into FY27 and leaving the INR370 crore base case intact; margin guidance of 25-26% for FY28 rests on capacity still to be built.

utilisation.quote: the existing facility operating at healthy utilization level

triggers.label: Price hike INR1.50 vs polymer cost INR2.25
triggers.quote: the selling price was increased by INR1.50

triggers.label: FY28 peak revenue INR425 cr, margin 25-26%

guidance.quote: we intend to take the commercial production in the last week of August
on annualized basis, we should be getting INR120 crores top line
we can still close at roughly 370 or so. INR370 crores.
SVP will get operational in March '27. So, that is on schedule.

guidance.value: FY27 about INR21 crores; FY28 INR18-19 crores

guidance.quote: our total depreciation will increase by about INR6 crores annually

summary.headline: Amanta Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~5% YoY to INR69 crore at ~22% EBITDA margin; SteriPort Line 3 commercial start slipped to late August.
summary.overview: Revenue grew about 5% YoY to roughly INR69 crore with EBITDA of about INR15 crore and margin near 22%, despite polymer cost spikes and pre-commissioning overheads. SteriPort Line 3 slipped from Q1 to Q2 FY27 due to civil construction delays; management now targets commercial production in the last week of August after FDA plan approval and an inspection scheduled for August 21. The SVP facility is now guided to commercialise around March 2027 (FAT in the US in November). Management guided to ~INR370 crore FY27 revenue without SVP and 25-26% EBITDA margin at peak utilisation for FY28.

financial_highlights.change: Marginal QoQ increase due to solar capex

segments.name: SteriPort (ISBM / BFS plastic containers)
segments.commentary: Contributes ~44% of revenue. Capacity expanding from 6.6 crore to ~12 crore bottles per year; Line 3 is a dedicated 500 ml platform, with ~INR120 crore annualised top line expected.

segments.name: SVP (small volume parenterals, export-centric)
segments.commentary: Around 20% of FY26 revenue; ~90% of SVP revenue is export, with over 60% from advanced/semi-advanced markets. New facility guided to March 2027, with 20 products in pipeline and first inhalation product targeted for commercialisation mid-September.

segments.name: Solar (captive)
segments.commentary: 10.8 MW captive solar plant commissioned June 2026; expected INR9 crore annual power cost saving.

guidance_outlook: SteriPort Line 3 commercial production targeted last week of August 2026, subject to FDA inspection on August 21; Q2 impact limited to about one month (September).
Line 3 annualised top line ~INR120 crore; FY27 (seven operating months from September) SteriPort contribution ~INR70 crore; FY27 baseline ~INR370 crore revenue excluding SVP.
FY28 peak revenue ~INR425 crore with all capacity live, at ~25-26% EBITDA margin (about +/-1%).
Console EBITDA margin expansion of 4-5% targeted post-Line 3, including ~INR9 crore solar saving.
Incremental depreciation ~INR6 crore annually vs FY26 (Line 3 ~INR4.5 crore plus SVP and solar); effective tax rate 26% in books.
Interest cost ~INR21 crore in FY27 and ~INR18-19 crore in FY28; debt to reduce by INR30-35 crore annually.
Polymer cost spike of 70-80% expected to be absorbed through price correction (INR1.50 price increase vs INR2.25 cost impact), with recovery spilling into the following quarter.
capex_capacity: SteriPort Line 3 total capex ~INR90 crore, of which ~INR80 crore spent; commercial production targeted late August 2026 after validation by ~18 August.
SVP facility capex ~INR30 crore, of which ~INR7 crore spent; FAT in USA in second week of November, site arrival by December, commercialisation around March 2027 (no major civil work).
Management estimates incremental ROCE of ~16-17% for SteriPort Line 3 and ~14-15% for SVP (analyst calculations confirmed as broadly right).
A separate formulation development centre is being built; F&D team of five scientists targeting 8-10 in F&D and 3-4 in regulatory affairs.
demand_pricing: Polymer prices rose ~70-80% during a roughly two-month spike linked to the Middle East crisis; prices have since eased close to earlier levels.
Management says the SteriPort-specific price increase was INR1.50 per unit against INR2.25 polymer cost impact; SteriPort polymer is a small part of its cost structure.
Management cited Iran war-related business slowdown across segments; Q1 growth attributed to product mix and better price realisation.
Domestic SteriPort competition named as Otsuka, Fresenius Kabi, B. Braun (major cities only) and Aculife.
SVP export markets: UK and Ireland the main advanced-market base; diluents previously exported to Australia and Canada; ophthalmics targeted for EU, Australia and Canada.
Management said SteriPort is at healthy utilisation (analyst noted 90-95%), and Line 3 is expected to absorb overheads and remove single-SKU constraints on the existing line.

qa_highlights.question: Will SteriPort Line 3 peak revenue of INR110-120 crore be realised within 12 months of commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR120 crore is an annualised figure with production capacity and net realisation unchanged; it expects the full annualised top line within 12 months from August-end commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Margin expansion of 3-4% after SteriPort: does it include the INR9 crore power saving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target was 5% expansion including the INR9 crore solar saving, so 4-5% console EBITDA margin expansion overall, driven by overhead absorption and a dedicated 500 ml line.

qa_highlights.question: What was the cost pressure in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly pre-commissioning overheads (staff hired ahead of Line 3) absorbed without contribution because commercialisation slipped one quarter, plus polymer price volatility of about 2-2.5 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 EBITDA outlook with SteriPort contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly INR70 crore of SteriPort top line in seven operating months (September onward) and FY27 baseline revenue of about INR370 crore without SVP.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex spend on Line 3 and SVP?
qa_highlights.answer: Line 3 total capex ~INR90 crore with ~INR80 crore spent; SVP total ~INR30 crore with ~INR7 crore spent to date.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle is long (15-25 days quarantine, more for exports); debt reducing INR30-35 crore annually; solar debt added temporarily, so downward trajectory of D/E should accelerate later.

risks_watch: SteriPort Line 3 start depends on FDA inspection on August 21 and validation completing around August 18; further slippage would defer contribution.
SVP commercialisation (March 2027) rests on FAT in November and on regulatory approvals; advanced-market approvals are slow and Annex 1 hardware corrections are pending for BFS.
Polymer and crude price volatility; recovery through price correction is lagging by about two quarters.
Rising interest and depreciation (~INR6 crore incremental) with debt-to-equity still at 1.06.
Working capital days at 141 remain high due to quarantine requirements; management has not given a target.
Management has not quantified R&D spend as a percentage of revenue and promised follow-up data.
key_quotes: So, that is a annualized number. So, the production capacity and the net realization that we envisage are not changing.
So, the margin pressure was not for 5 months. In this 5 months, the polymer spike was there for maybe 45 days or 2 months nearly.
I, honestly, I have not quantified, I don't have the numbers with me at this moment, but earlier, we did not have dedicated F&D department.
But if you increase price by INR1.75 -- INR1.50, even if it has to come down, it may come down by INR0.25 or INR0.30, but it will remain INR1 plus for longer time.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the medium-term growth story (SteriPort capacity, SVP, solar), but cautious on timelines, repeatedly tying SteriPort Line 3 start to the FDA inspection on August 21 and SVP to a March 2027 date. Management was evasive on R&D spend (not quantified, follow-up promised) and gave no working capital days target.

adds.what: SteriPort Line 3 dedicated 500 ml ISBM/BFS platform (capacity expanding from 6.6 crore to ~12 crore bottles/yr)
SVP new facility (export-centric small volume parenterals)

growth.why: Management guides ~INR370 cr FY27 revenue excluding SVP (about 7 operating months of Line 3 from September, ~INR70 cr contribution) and FY28 peak ~INR425 cr at 25-26% margin, backed by SteriPort Line 3 (INR80 cr of INR90 cr capex spent, commercial start late August, FDA inspection Aug 21) and SVP (March 2027), but the Line 3 slip and lack of firm order numbers keep backing partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: post-Line 3 stabilisation, H2 FY27 into FY28
rows.why: Management targets 4-5% console EBITDA margin expansion after Line 3 including ~INR9 crore solar saving, and FY28 margin of 25-26% vs ~22% in Q1 FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (SteriPort Line 3, late August 2026); Q4 FY27 (SVP,
rows.why: SteriPort Line 3 is ~INR80 crore of INR90 crore spent with commercial production targeted last week of August subject to FDA inspection on August 21; SVP is ~INR7 crore of INR30 crore spent with commercialisation guided to March 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: Q3 FY27 onward, ramping to FY28 peak
rows.why: SteriPort capacity expands from 6.6 crore to ~12 crore bottles/yr with Line 3 at ~INR120 crore annualised top line; FY27 SteriPort contribution ~INR70 crore over seven operating months; FY28 peak revenue ~INR425 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is described as healthy (analyst read 90-95% for SteriPort), but Line 3 and SVP are already under construction, and a separate formulation development centre is being built, so any new announcement depends on Line 3 ramp-up and debt reduction of INR30-35 crore annually.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is ~INR370 crore FY27 revenue excluding SVP with a Q2 impact of only about one month, and Q1 revenue grew only ~5% YoY with pre-commissioning overheads absorbed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Line 3 start depends on FDA inspection on August 21 and validation by ~August 18, and the Line 3 start has already slipped one quarter; SVP commercialisation depends on November FAT and approvals.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First inhalation product from SVP is targeted for commercialisation mid-September, with 20 products in the SVP pipeline, though SVP is ~20% of FY26 revenue and ~90% export.

rows.label: FDA inspection for SteriPort Line 3 on August 21, 2026
rows.why: Line 3 commercial start (~INR120 crore annualised top line) depends on this inspection, and validation is due around August 18 after the one-quarter slip.

rows.label: Captive solar saving of INR9 crore per year
rows.why: 10.8 MW captive solar commissioned June 2026 with ~INR75 lakh per month saving, adding about 4-5% to console EBITDA margin with Line 3.

rows.label: Debt reduction of INR30-35 crore annually
rows.why: Debt-to-equity has declined to 1.06 in FY26, interest cost is guided at ~INR21 crore in FY27 and INR18-19 crore in FY28, and solar debt is temporarily added.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term story (Line 3 capacity, SVP, solar, FY28 INR425 crore peak) but cautious on timelines tied to the August 21 FDA inspection and March 2027 SVP date; it was evasive on R&D spend and gave no working capital target, while analysts pressed on the margin bridge
